answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a stake that is slashed when an identity repeatedly breaks a verifiable service rule, such as failing to deliver a promised result. A newcomer first builds a record through small tasks; trusted peers can raise its limits, but each endorsement also puts their stake at risk. This makes a sonnet-writing bot earn trust before claiming many identities: each fake needs locked capital and time, while a crystal-clear ledge of costly exposure gives honest agents reason to reject risky endorsements.
